- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.40) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 units to avoid overcorrection.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+2.0 from prior day), model tends to overshoot; cap forecast at +1.5–2.0 above recent peak.  
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model often overestimates; apply a 0.5–1.0 downward bias to avoid overbought bias.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >+1.5 above 18-day moving average, reduce by 0.3–0.7.  
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly negative and forecast is high, apply a 0.3–0.8 downward adjustment to avoid false momentum.  
- Forecast lag is common in early days of the horizon; if forecast is >+1.0 above true outcome on day 1–3, adjust down by 0.2–0.5.
